issues.t: Automatic transmission slips, shudders or fails
issues.sym: Slipping between gears, shuddering, harsh or delayed shifts, a whine when accelerating, or a 'Transmission Service Urgent' message. Some cars stop moving altogether.
issues.why: The automatic transmissions in the first-generation S80, especially the GM-built unit used in early T6 models, are its most common serious failure. Owners report worn internals, shift solenoid faults and full failures, often between 50,000 and 120,000 miles. 1999 is considered the worst year.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and have a Volvo specialist read the transmission codes. Ask about software updates first; a solenoid or valve body repair may avoid a full rebuild.

issues.t: Throttle module causes stalling and limp mode
issues.sym: Rough idle, stalling in traffic, sudden loss of power, a no-start, or a warning light with the car in reduced-power limp mode.
issues.why: Early S80s use an electronic throttle module whose internal contacts wear and get dirty. Volvo paid for cleanings and many replacements, and changed the design and supplier during the 2002 model year.
issues.next: Have the throttle codes read. Cleaning sometimes helps, but a worn module needs replacing. Ask a Volvo dealer whether any goodwill coverage applies to your car.

issues.t: ABS module fails and turns on warning lights
issues.sym: ABS, brake and traction (TRACS/STC) warning lights come on, sometimes on and off, and often worse in cold weather. The anti-lock system may stop working.
issues.why: Solder joints on the ABS control module's circuit board crack over time and lose contact.
issues.next: Normal brakes still work, but ABS may not. Have the codes read and rule out a wheel speed sensor first; the module can usually be rebuilt rather than replaced.

issues.t: Clogged PCV oil trap causes oil leaks
issues.sym: Oil leaks around the engine, seals pushed out, oil smoke or pressure at the dipstick, whistling at idle, or higher oil use.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) oil trap and hoses clog with sludge. Pressure then builds inside the engine and pushes oil past seals. Breather box seal leaks are common on the T6.
issues.next: Have the PCV system checked and cleaned or replaced, ideally around 100,000 miles. Fixing it early can prevent seal and turbo damage.

issues.t: Worn front control arm bushings
issues.sym: Clunking over bumps, loose or wandering steering, vibration when braking, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: The rubber bushings in the front lower control arms tear and wear out at higher mileage. Tie rods and ball joints wear too.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected. Replace worn arms or bushings in pairs and get an alignment.

issues.t: Worn struts and strut mounts
issues.sym: A bouncy or floaty ride, knocking over bumps, or oil on the strut body.
issues.why: The struts and their upper mounts wear out on high-mileage cars and are among the most reported S80 repairs.
issues.next: Have the struts and mounts checked. Replace them in pairs on the same axle.

issues.t: Worn engine mounts cause vibration
issues.sym: Extra vibration at idle or in gear, and a clunk when accelerating or shifting.
issues.why: The right-side and upper engine mounts wear out or leak their fluid.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected. A worn torque or upper mount is fairly simple to replace.

issues.t: Ignition coil failure causes misfires
issues.sym: A check engine light, rough running or shaking, and loss of power.
issues.why: Individual ignition coils fail on the six-cylinder engines and are often replaced one at a time.
issues.next: Have the misfire code read to find the cylinder and replace that coil. Don't drive long with a flashing check engine light.

issues.t: Radiator and coolant hose leaks
issues.sym: Coolant puddles, a sweet smell, a low coolant warning, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: Plastic radiator necks, hoses and cores crack with age on early cars.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and have it pressure tested. Stop driving if the engine overheats.

issues.t: Turbo oil return line seals leak
issues.sym: Oil dripping under the engine, oil smell or smoke from the exhaust area.
issues.why: The O-rings on the turbo oil drain tubes harden and leak on the twin-turbo T6.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. Replacing both drain tube O-rings takes several hours but is much less work than replacing a turbo.

issues.t: Xenon headlight fails or aims wrong
issues.sym: One headlight goes out or flickers, or a headlight warning appears.
issues.why: Bulbs, HID ballast modules and leveling parts fail on higher-mileage cars.
issues.next: Check the bulb first, then the ballast module. Use matching parts so beams stay correctly aimed.

issues.t: A/C stops blowing cold
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, cuts in and out, or the compressor clutch doesn't engage.
issues.why: Compressor clutches, compressors and refrigerant lines wear out.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks and pressures before recharging.

issues.t: Central electronic module (CEM) faults
issues.sym: Random problems with windows, locks, wipers, lights or gauges, warning lights, or a no-start from the immobilizer.
issues.why: The CEM controls most body electronics. Water leaks, corroded connections or a weak battery can make it misbehave.
issues.next: Test the battery and grounds first and fix any water leak. A Volvo specialist can repair or reprogram the CEM.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms until a crash.
issues.why: The driver's airbag inflator propellant can degrade, so the inflator may burst and throw metal fragments (recalls 20V-681 and 21V-766).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free airbag replacement right away.

issues.t: Oil leaks from vacuum pump and valve cover
issues.sym: Oil on the side or front of the engine, burning oil smell, or drips under the car.
issues.why: The vacuum pump seals on the 3.2L blow out, and the valve cover sealant ages on both six-cylinder engines.
issues.next: Have the leak cleaned and traced. Reseal the vacuum pump or valve cover before oil reaches belts or exhaust.

issues.t: Hissing at idle from torn PCV diaphragm
issues.sym: A hiss or whistle at idle, rough idle, or a check engine light.
issues.why: The rubber diaphragm in the T6's PCV valve tears and lets in unmetered air.
issues.next: Have the PCV valve checked; replacing it is a fairly small job.

issues.t: Water pump and accessory pulley wear
issues.sym: Coolant leaks, a whirring noise or wobbling pulley at the front of the engine, or overheating.
issues.why: On the six-cylinder engines the accessory drive pulley wears and strains its bearings, and early water pumps leak. Cooling hose O-rings also dry out.
issues.next: Have the belt drive and water pump inspected at higher mileage, and fix coolant leaks before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Engine burns oil from piston ring wear
issues.sym: Needing to add oil between changes, white or blue exhaust smoke, and a rough idle.
issues.why: Six-cylinder engines built before 2012 used pistons and rings that let oil burn. Volvo later redesigned them.
issues.next: Track oil use carefully and keep it topped up. If consumption is severe, ask a Volvo dealer for an oil consumption test.

issues.t: Low oil level warning from faulty dipstick
issues.sym: An 'Engine Oil Level Low' message and apparent oil loss.
issues.why: A faulty dipstick lets oil vapor escape. Volvo service bulletin TJ30021 replaces the dipstick and updates engine software.
issues.next: Check the oil and ask a dealer if TJ30021 applies to your car.

issues.t: AWD system disabled warning (Haldex pump)
issues.sym: An 'AWD Disabled Service Required' message, AWD warning light, and the car drives in front-wheel drive only.
issues.why: The Haldex rear coupling's pump and filter clog with clutch material, or the pump or its control module fail. Mismatched tires can also trigger it.
issues.next: Have the AWD codes read. A fluid and filter service often fixes it; keep all four tires matched.

issues.t: Adaptive (Four-C) shocks leak or fail
issues.sym: A harsher or bouncier ride, a suspension warning, or leaking shocks.
issues.why: Electronically adjustable shocks on these cars wear out over time.
issues.next: Have the shocks inspected. Non-adaptive conversion kits are an option on older cars.

issues.t: A/C compressor fails
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, or there's a grinding or rumbling from the compressor.
issues.why: Compressor bearings and compressors fail on these years.
issues.next: Turn the A/C off if it's noisy and have it checked before the bearing seizes.

issues.t: Tire pressure sensor valve stems crack
issues.sym: A tire pressure warning, or a tire slowly losing air at the valve.
issues.why: The aluminum valve stems on the tire pressure sensors corrode and crack.
issues.next: Have the tire shop replace the stem or sensor; ask for a new valve kit whenever tires are changed.

issues.t: V8 valve cover oil leaks
issues.sym: Burning oil smell, smoke from the engine bay, or oil on the engine.
issues.why: Valve cover gaskets on the 4.4L V8 leak with age.
issues.next: Have the leak traced and the gaskets replaced before oil drips onto the exhaust.

issues.t: Front seat belt anchor cable can break (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms.
issues.why: The steel cable that connects the seat belt to the front seats can wear from fatigue and break, so the belt may not hold you in a crash (recall 20V-378).
issues.next: Check your VIN and get the free cable replacement.

issues.t: Wipers may stop or run by themselves (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers don't work or turn on without being switched on.
issues.why: Diagnostic software in the central electronic module can upset wiper operation (recall 09V-139).
issues.next: Have the free CEM software update done.

issues.t: Cooling fan may stop and engine can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Temperature gauge rising, overheating warning.
issues.why: A software error in the fan control module can stop the cooling fan (recall 09V-218).
issues.next: Stop if it overheats and get the free software update.

issues.t: Fuel pump may not start and engine stalls (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or won't start.
issues.why: Central electronic module software can fail to signal the fuel pump module (recall 09V-343).
issues.next: Get the free software update.

issues.t: Driver airbag clockspring connector fault (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag (SRS) warning light.
issues.why: An intermittent fault in the driver airbag clockspring connector means the airbag may not deploy correctly (recall 10V-489).
issues.next: Get the free repair.

issues.t: Engine can stall suddenly from software fuel cut-off (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can shut off while driving.
issues.why: Fuel cut-off calibration in the engine computer was too sensitive (recall 10V-579).
issues.next: Get the free engine and transmission software update.

issues.t: Engine can stall when coasting from transmission software (recall)
issues.sym: RPM drops and the engine may stall when coasting to a stop.
issues.why: Transmission software may not downshift while coasting (recall 12V-317).
issues.next: Get the free transmission software update.

issues.t: Seat wiring can disconnect and affect airbags (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light, especially after moving the seat.
issues.why: A wiring harness under the front seats may not be clipped to the frame and can come apart (recall 12V-075).
issues.next: Get the free inspection and repair.

issues.t: False tire pressure service message (recall)
issues.sym: A 'TPMS Service Required' message after driving, and no warning for low tires.
issues.why: A software error disables low-pressure warnings (recall 12V-415).
issues.next: Check tire pressures by hand and get the free reprogramming.

issues.t: Wipers run nonstop and lights can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers run continuously; turn signals, high beams or headlight switch stop working.
issues.why: Central electronic module software fault on cars with keyless ignition (recall 13V-377).
issues.next: Get the free CEM software update.

issues.t: Starter fuse can blow with stop/start (recall)
issues.sym: The engine won't restart after an auto stop.
issues.why: The starter fuse may blow with stop/start use (recall 15V-555).
issues.next: Get the free higher-rated fuse installed.
